goal: Add native Compact source obligations, compiler relation and artifact pins, cost ceilings and mutation verification
asset: Proof, statement, mutation and cost ratchets with pinned native Midnight verification
scope: Compact source escape hatches and circuit obligation identities
Pinned compactc/runtime/ledger compilation and generated relation/artifact freshness
Real native verifier positive/negative controls and per-circuit measured ceilings
Isolated circuit assert/comparison/disclosure mutants through the real proof-test adapter
outOfScope: Automatic toolchain installation in consumer projects
Claiming JavaScript ledger WASM verifies cryptographic proofs
Network deployment or real user witnesses

record.question: How should Compact obligations be checked without treating simulation or arbitrary process success as native proof verification?

options.strongest_objection: Requires a project-owned generated-state/proof driver and native verifier toolchain
Cannot detect changed compiled relations, verifier pins or native proof test gaps

record.rationale: Keep source ratchets cheap and explicit while a separate fail-closed adapter compiles pinned circuits, validates actual native request controls and measures artifact/IR costs. Mutants run in independent snapshots against the same adapter.
evidence: Issue #185 names immutable ledger-8 deployment obligations
Official compactc0.31.1 release SHA256 verified and native compiler executed
Orynq SDK pins native ledger8.1.3 proof-verifying and real proof fixture controls

costs.cost: Maintain a small Python adapter, source scanner and native test recipe
evidence: Public compiler/SRS pins and native ledger proof fixture are available

costs.cost: Native proof, relation and cost changes remain unchecked
evidence: Issue #185 gap and existing scanner suffix inventory

requirements.statement: Count Compact TODO, constant asserts, exported circuits without assertions and unjustified disclosures without counting quoted prose; circuit signatures/assertions have statement identities
requirements.counterexample: An assert is deleted or disclose added without a source/statement ratchet change

requirements.statement: Tracked stateful/witness Compact tokens require complete manifest coverage and explicitly declared native proof checks require arming; pinned compiler, runtime and ledger identity produce nonempty expected proof circuits; exact normalized IR and generated code/key/state pins and measured cost ceilings reject drift; native positive and negative controls must complete with expected verified outcomes
requirements.counterexample: Simulation or a zero-exit no-op passes, a key or relation changes, or a metric exceeds its ceiling

requirements.statement: Compile isolated assert/comparison/disclosure mutants and score only viable complete proof-test outcomes after a passing native baseline, preserving clean HEAD and existing mutation ratchet semantics
requirements.counterexample: A failed baseline, unviable mutant or incomplete native run is published as a killed mutant

checks.scope: Adapter protocol, isolation, source/statement scanner and existing mutation CLI routing; separate actual compiler/native fixture runs recorded in evidence
assumptions: Project proof driver and pinned native verifier are reviewed trusted programs; protocol fixtures validate adapter enforcement, not cryptographic implementation

challenges.claim: Does the JavaScript ledger flag verify real proofs?
challenges.resolution: No. Native verification must use the pinned ledger build with proof-verifying and without mock-verify; native controls distinguish actual valid and corrupted proof requests.

challenges.claim: Can source-only scanner changes close this feature?
challenges.resolution: No. Actual compiler/native positive and mutant-negative evidence is required before calling the native adapter complete.
